1. Introduction
This report presents the design and implementation of WebTrace Insight Lab: Website
Network Behavior Fingerprinting System, an academic computer networks project
developed to observe, capture, and analyze the network behavior of websites using packet-
level metadata.
In modern web communication, most website traffic is encrypted using HTTPS. Because of
this, directly reading application-layer payloads is neither practical nor ethical for a basic
educational project. Instead of inspecting private content, this project focuses on passive
metadata-based network analysis. It studies packet sizes, timing, protocols, transfer volume,
and traffic direction to understand how websites behave at the network level.

The system captures live traffic from the local machine while a user accesses a target
website. It then extracts meaningful features, generates a behavioral fingerprint, classifies
the website traffic pattern, compares different captures, and displays the results through a
web-based dashboard.
2. Scope of the Project
The scope of this project includes the following:
Capturing live network packets from the local system using Scapy.
Allowing the user to enter a website URL for observation.
Capturing packets during a user-defined time window.
Extracting packet-level metadata such as IP addresses, ports, protocols, packet sizes, and
timestamps.
Calculating traffic statistics such as total packets, total bytes, average packet size, and
packets per second.
Generating a unique fingerprint for each website capture.

3. Project Objectives
The main objectives of this project are:
To capture live network traffic generated while accessing a website.
To extract useful packet metadata without reading private payloads.
To identify protocol usage such as TCP, UDP, DNS, ICMP, and other packet types.
To calculate traffic metrics such as packet count, byte count, packet size, packet
frequency, and directionality.

To identify protocol usage such as TCP, UDP, DNS, ICMP, and other packet types.
To calculate traffic metrics such as packet count, byte count, packet size, packet
frequency, and directionality.
To generate a unique behavioral fingerprint for a website.
To classify website behavior into meaningful categories such as media-heavy,
lightweight, or API-driven.
To compare two website captures and calculate a similarity score.
To visualize network behavior using graphs and charts.
To provide a user-friendly web interface for computer networks lab work.
To demonstrate passive network analysis in an ethical and educational way.

5. Dataset Description
5.1 Data Source
The project uses two types of data sources: Live Packet Sniffing (captured from the local
machine when the user enters a website URL) and Demo Mode Static Dataset (stored in
JSON format, useful when administrator privileges are not available).

6. System Architecture
The project follows a modular multi-layer architecture including the Packet Capture Layer,
Analysis Layer, Storage Layer, Backend/API Layer, and Frontend Layer.
7. Conclusion
The WebTrace Insight Lab successfully demonstrates passive computer network analysis
using live packet sniffing and metadata-based behavior profiling. The system captures
packets using Scapy, extracts important network features, generates a unique fingerprint,
classifies website behavior, compares captures, and displays results through an interactive
web dashboard. Overall, WebTrace Insight Lab is a useful computer networks lab project
that connects theoretical networking concepts with practical real-world traffic observation.
